### Summary of Fix for Issue [#288](https://github.com/matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation/issues/288)

**PR:** [matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation#289](https://github.com/matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation/pull/289)  
**Branch:** `fix/issue-288-portal-ux-show-loading-please-wait-splas`  
**Classification:** T1 (`engineer:needs-fix`)  

---

### Root Cause & Approach
The device web portal serves 11 gzipped PROGMEM assets sequentially over HTTP/1.1 from the ESP32. During asset transfer and initial REST API roundtrips (~3–5s waterfall), the browser previously displayed a blank or partially-rendered page without indication that the device was actively responding.

To resolve this perceived-performance gap without affecting backend logic or C++ runtime APIs:
1. **Inline HTML Splash (`web/portal/index.html`):** Inlined `<div id="loading-splash">` directly at the top of `<body>` with an animated spinner and "Loading, please wait…" text equipped with accessible ARIA semantics (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`).
2. **Critical Inline CSS (`web/portal/index.html`):** Inlined splash styles in `<style>` inside `<head>` preceding `app.css` to guarantee immediate rendering during the first TCP response. Includes fallbacks for light/dark themes (`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`) and motion accessibility (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`).
3. **Design System Integration (`web/portal/app.css`):** Integrated `#loading-splash` CSS tokens to inherit theme variables (`--bg`, `--text`, `--text-muted`) once `app.css` arrives, with `body.portal-ready #loading-splash { display: none !important; }`.
4. **Clean DOM Dismissal (`web/portal/app.js`):** Added `dismissLoadingSplash()` to safely remove `#loading-splash` from the DOM once boot completes and `portal-ready` is set on `document.body` (handled across both standard and error fallback boot paths).
5. **Asset Compilation (`scripts/portalBuilder.py`):** Rebuilt PROGMEM headers (`include/portal_assets/index_html.hpp`, `app_css.hpp`, `app_js.hpp`), resulting in an increase of only +519 gzipped bytes.
6. **Automated Tests (`test/web/tests/smoke.spec.ts`):** Added Playwright tests verifying the splash is visible during delayed boot and cleanly dismissed when `portal-ready` is reached.
